cases.rehabilitation_interpretation: Current staged hip-and-knee flexion, high-flexion hold, and staged return task.
Same staged assisted flexion-return task performed over a moderate range of motion.
The same full high-flexion rehabilitation task performed at a deliberately slower clinical pace.
Assisted hip-flexion or straight-leg-raise-like task with the knee kept near extension but not at the singular zero-flexion posture.
Isolated assisted knee flexion-extension with the thigh comparatively stabilized.
Two ordinary moderate flexion-return repetitions in one session rather than one staged high-flexion repetition.

recommended_next_research_step: Pre-register replication across a small fixed set of patient mismatches and measurement seeds with the same six trajectories and unchanged controller/trust contract; do not add active excitation or retune trajectories within this evidence set.

relationships.caution: n=6 preregistered trajectories, with promotion-timing relationships restricted to promoted cases; correlations are descriptive only, not inferential or a calibrated dose-response

scientific_conclusion.scope_limit: simulation/engineering evidence for one registered perturbed Human, one measurement seed, and one MPC seed
scientific_conclusion.statement: Natural rehabilitation motion supported valid one-shot promotion in five of six trajectories for this single patient and sensor realization. Poorer practical conditioning was associated with later promotion and less remaining trajectory among promoted cases, but excitation strength did not monotonically determine prediction or tracking benefit. One shared force-gate termination prevented candidate formation and cannot be attributed solely to identifiability.

scope: single registered perturbed Human, single registered sensor/noise realization, simulation/engineering evidence only
